# What Is Quarto?

## Why are we here?

By the end of this hour you will be able to:

- Explain what [Quarto]{.uwred} is and how it works with R and RStudio
- Write a report that mixes text and R code
- Render it to a self-contained file and publish it online
- Turn the same kind of document into a [slide deck]{.uwred}
- Write a [manuscript]{.uwred} with citations and cross-references

<div class="gap-md"></div>

You'll build along with me the whole hour, with a few [Your turn]{.uwred} moments to try a step on your own.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## What is Quarto?

[Quarto]{.uwred} is a free, open-source publishing system.

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

You write one plain-text file (a `.qmd`) that mixes:

- Text, written in [markdown]{.uwred}
- Code, in R or Python
- A few options at the top, written in [YAML]{.uwred}

<div class="gap-md"></div>

Quarto turns that file into a finished document:

- Reports (HTML, Word, PDF)
- Slide decks
- Manuscripts and journal articles


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## R, RStudio, and Quarto

Three tools, three different jobs:

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

| Tool | What it is | Its job |
|---|---|---|
| [R]{.uwred} (or Python) | A programming language | Runs your code: data, models, figures |
| [RStudio]{.uwred} | An IDE | Where you write code and documents |
| [Quarto]{.uwred} | A publishing system | Turns your `.qmd` into a finished document |

: {tbl-colwidths="[20,30,50]"}

<div class="gap-md"></div>

You use them together: write a `.qmd` in RStudio, [render]{.uwred} it from the terminal, and Quarto has R run your code and builds the document around the results.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## What happens when you render

```bash
quarto render report.qmd
```

```{mermaid}
%%| echo: false
flowchart LR
  Q[".qmd<br/>text + code"] --> E["engine<br/>runs the code"]
  E --> M[".md<br/>text + results"]
  M --> P["Pandoc<br/>converts"]
  P --> O["HTML, Word,<br/>PDF, slides"]
```

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

- An [engine]{.uwred} runs your code chunks: knitr for R, Jupyter for Python
- Your numbers, tables, and figures are woven into the text
- [Pandoc]{.uwred} converts the result to the format you asked for

<div class="gap-md"></div>

The engine runs your code in a [fresh session]{.uwred}, not in your RStudio console. Remember this; it matters in the next unit.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Why use Quarto?

| The old way | With Quarto |
|---|---|
| Copy numbers from the console into Word, then they drift out of date when the data change | Text and code live together; numbers are computed every time you render |
| Rebuild the same figure for the report, the slides, and the paper | One source, many formats |
| Type citations by hand and renumber figures when you reorder them | Citations come from a `.bib` file; figure and table numbers update themselves |
| "How did I get this result?" | Rendering re-runs everything from scratch, so the document *is* the record |
| Binary files that Git can't compare | Plain text that works with Git |


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## A few quick notes

[Quarto is its own program.]{.uwred} Like Git, you run it from the terminal, and every command starts with `quarto`. It works the same whether you edit in RStudio, Positron, VS Code, or Jupyter.

<div class="gap-md"></div>

[It is not just for R.]{.uwred} If your project uses Python, you can use Quarto the same way. Code chunks just say `{python}` instead of `{r}`.

<div class="gap-md"></div>

[Coming from R Markdown?]{.uwred} Quarto is its successor. Most of what you know carries over, and your `.Rmd` files still work.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Source vs. output

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

| File | What it is | What you do with it |
|---|---|---|
| `report.qmd` | The [source]{.uwred} | Write and edit it; commit it to Git |
| `report.html` | The [output]{.uwred} | Read and share it; never edit it by hand |

<div class="gap-md"></div>

Quarto rebuilds the output from scratch every time you render, so any edits you make to the HTML will be overwritten.

<div class="gap-md"></div>

To change the output, change the source and render again.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Where we are

We have:

- Defined Quarto as a publishing system, separate from R and RStudio
- Seen what happens when you render
- Seen why it beats copy and paste for reports, slides, and papers
